ContainerSnapshot.description:
Selected inspection evidence. Environment variables, labels and host paths
never enter a plan. The full ID, image and start timestamp identify an instance.

DeclaredOutcome.description:
What the administrator declares about the job. Only `AcceptedDivergence`
rests on the operator's word; the other two are checked against evidence.

oneOf.description: The intended end state is present on every target.
Nothing took effect: every target still equals the plan's `expected`.
The present state differs from both before and intended; accepted.

code.description:
The error that describes the current state: for the observation
runtime, the one that ended its latest run; for the storage reader,
`unavailable` for a stuck read and `forbidden` for a socket core
refuses; for the store, `unavailable`.

count.description:
For the observation runtime, failures in the current run; it restarts
after a longer wait each time. For the storage reader, reads stuck
(0 for a refused socket).
For the store, calls waiting for its writer.

since.description:
When the current state began (Unix seconds): for the storage reader,
when its oldest stuck read was abandoned, or when core first refused
its socket; for the store, when its
writer started the item it is still on.

detail.description:
What is wrong and since when. Given to an authenticated caller and to
`limeosctl status`; the unauthenticated health check names only the
subsystem.

oneOf.description:
The container executor refused an execute request for an action it
holds no receipt for, because the plan expires at or below its prune
watermark: a receipt for it may have been pruned, so the executor can
no longer tell whether the action already ran. Never retried as an
effect. Fresh plans meet it only after the clock stepped back by more
than the receipt retention period, until the clock catches up.

The container executor refused an execute request because a container
it would act on has spent its effect budget (ADR 0013): refused before
the store writes any receipt for the action, so nothing ran or can run
for it. Settled as refused, never retried as an effect.

EventKind.description: Authority events contain stable types and identifiers, never credentials.

oneOf.description:
The executor answered that it holds no receipt for this job, after its
receipt may have been pruned: whether the action ran is unknown, and the
job stays held for an operator.

The container executor's receipt store changed while this job was held:
an answer carried a store epoch other than the one core last saw (a
store reopened, lost and recreated, or restored from an older copy).
The store may have lost what this job did, so a `never_recorded`
closure for it is not accepted.

The executor answered with a closure saying it never recorded this job,
which contradicts what core holds: a result core already recorded, or
a dispatch under an earlier store epoch. Nothing was released; the job
stays held for an operator.

The container executor refused the job's execute because a container
it would act on has spent its effect budget (ADR 0013): nothing ran,
and the job is settled as refused. `frees_at` is when, by the
executor's clock, every such container has room again.

An open resolution request was closed without effect: the job had
already settled by another path (recovery recorded the executor's
receipt or closure) as `state`, so the request could never complete.

The host operator cancelled this queued job on its owner's behalf
(`limeosctl job cancel`, a root peer naming an administrator). The
event's principal is that administrator; the owner's history shows
the `canceled` transition, written in the same transaction.

Stack aggregate only: every sent member is verified and every other
member is provably unsent. Terminal; never reported as success.

JobResolution.description:
The completed audit record (step 3). Additional to, never replacing, the
job's `outcome_unknown`/`needs_intervention` history.

oneOf.description:
An administrator settled an uncertain job on evidence. Terminal and
lock-releasing; the original job, plan and receipts stay unchanged.

MaintenanceWindow.description: UTC minutes. Start is inclusive, end exclusive; a crossing window spans midnight.

NeedsAttentionJob.description:
One stuck container or stack job in the administrator-wide attention list.
Read-only: it names the job and its owner, never evidence or a decision.

created_at.description: Unix seconds of the job's first recorded event; 0 when none survives.

owner.description: Username of the principal that created the job.

state.description: `needs_intervention`, or `running`/`verifying` left by an earlier core.

targets.description: Resources the action would touch, as `container:<id>`.

ResolutionEvidence.description:
Evidence for exactly the job's targets, sorted by container ID. Core and
executor build it with the same function so their digests agree.

ResolutionMember.description:
One target's outcome as the executor recorded it in the job's receipt. For
a container job there is exactly one; for a stack, one per member.

container.description: Full container ID, without the `container:` prefix.

ResolutionRequest.description:
A recorded request (step 1). The job stays locked until the executor has
confirmed and core has completed it.

ResolutionTarget.description:
One target's fresh, read-only measurement against the plan. A container
that no longer exists is recorded with empty `image` and `started_at`,
`running` false and both flags false (see `is_absent`).

container.description: Full container ID, without the `container:` prefix.

intended_state_reached.description: The plan's action is proven by this target's post-state.

matches_expected.description: ID, start time, image and running state all equal the plan's `expected`.

expected.description: What the plan expected before the action.

measured.description: What a read-only inspection found just now.

digest binds a later decision to exactly what was shown.

ResolveKind.description: Which executor table holds the action: one container or a whole stack.

oneOf.description: HTTP 200. The executor and core both released the job.

HTTP 202. The request is recorded and the job stays held; the executor
was unreachable or its answer was lost. Core retries on its own, and the
same POST may be repeated.

HTTP 409. The state changed since the evidence was shown. Nothing is
held; `view` carries the fresh evidence.

HTTP 409. The evidence does not support `declared`; `blocking` names the
targets that differ and `view` carries the evidence.

settled_through.description: Last atomically settled occurrence, including skipped/blocked ones.

StackFileStatus.description: Diagnostic facts only. No variant makes stack actions executable.

oneOf.description:
A container of this project was left out of the read (changing,
unsupported or truncated), so its membership is incomplete and it is

Some Engine container's Compose labels could not be read, so whether it
belongs to or overlaps this stack is unknown. Every stack carries it and
none is planned.

StackOmissionReason.description: Why one inspected Engine container is not among the members.

oneOf.description: Its identity-relevant facts differed between the two inspections.
A mount type, label set or name this reader does not model.

catalog_stack.description: The registered catalog stack name; may differ from the Compose project.

StackReceipt.description:
`state` is always the aggregate of `members`, which lists exactly the
plan's targets. A member that was never sent is `precondition_changed`.

StackSnapshot.description: Every ordinary (non one-off) member, stopped or running, sorted by ID.

valid_for_millis.description: Remaining display lifetime, shortened by every cache/transport layer.

StorageFstabEntry.description:
Only identity/target fields leave the protected reader. Fstab options may
contain credentials and are never copied into RPC, plans or HTTP responses.

StorageMountWaitPlan.description: A requested wait on a filesystem assignment, never on its media subdirectories.

Subsystem.description: A part of the service that can fail on its own while core keeps serving.

oneOf.description: The 1 Hz health-observation and automation runtime.

The storage reader has a storage read stuck past its deadline (a
failing disk, typically); it refuses storage inventory until the read
returns and serves everything else. Or core refuses the reader's
socket (code `forbidden`): it is not served by the reader's own
account from its runtime directory (`ExecutorOwner`), so core takes
no storage, stack or container-health answer from it.

The store's single writer thread has been on one item for too long
(a hung fsync, a lock held from outside), or did not answer a probe
in time. Requests that need the store fail at their deadline
meanwhile, and core reports itself not ready.
